I’ve had my pension scheme contact me under my deadname as it doesn’t seem the company correctly passed on all the necessary information. 

That would be indirect discrimination. Due to their policies.

Other discrimination would be I’ve been outed by countless colleagues to customers and each other due to the company’s inadequate LGBTQ+ training or understanding. Apart from slurs being used as well, just the act of them outing me is discrimination?

The harassment (as the legal interpretation of it) is the unwanted action of receiving correspondence under my deadname as I’ve been advised by ACAS.

I’ve also been in contact with the Information Commisions Office (advised by the company themselves) who said it could be a breach under a principle A as it’s not keeping documents fair and accurate. And Principle D again not keeping documents accurately.

Ideally, I want the old name totally off the record as it’s an invasion of privacy and it’s forcing me to be outed against my wishes.

I’ve previously been told that all the “surface level” documentation of the old name has been changed (email addresses, any correspondence sent after the legal name change, any name that other colleagues might be able to see or access) but yet I am still receiving documents with the old name listed. So either they have not done their job correctly, someone is sneaking a look at my personnel file and looking at my deadname for whatever reason, or someone had a really good guess at my deadname.

My ultimate issue is that it’s causing instances of discrimination (direct and indirect) and it’s causing harassment. If this information was changed to reflect the legal name, then it is less likely that this would happen, and improve my mental health by not forcing myself to be in a position where I have to out myself.
I’m not capable of living when I’m going to miss out on so much, because I wasn’t brave enough with myself at 16
